correctness.rationale: At fixed n,k the only needed count is H=number of scattered 01 pairs; H=Σ_j j w_j−binom(k,2) in zero-based indexing. Advancing the rotation start by one changes H by n w_i−k, so equal values require equal starts modulo L=n/g. For any nonempty subset of one start group, the selected starts share a value exactly when each arc between successive selected starts contains d_jK ones. The arcs partition all labeled positions, and the probability is the product of binomial coefficients over the fixed-weight denominator. Inside an equality block of size a, summing (−1)^{r+1} binom(a,r) over nonempty subsets of the block gives one; this proves the expectation without any independence assumption across collisions or start groups. Equality at the global minimum forces every length-L window to contain K ones, so sliding one place gives w_{i+L}=w_i; the converse and g=1 follow. For g=3 the three pair events have equal probability p, all pair-event intersections are the same triple event of probability q, and the singleton, double and triple contributions yield the displayed multiplicities. Uniform Stirling for fixed g and interior density gives order L^{−(r−1)/2} for r specified starts in one group; hence only pairs affect the √L term. An unordered pair sum equals g/2 times the sum over its g−1 directed separations, giving the coefficient and the uniform O(1) remainder. An independent finite check computed all six signature counts at all rotations of every one of the 84 labeled length-nine weight-three words and compared them with the positional moment and window period test. It found counts of words 3,18,36,18,9 at diversity 3,4,5,6,7 respectively, and mean 36/7 (p=15/28, q=9/28); the finite check is not evidence for uniform asymptotics apart from the proof.
residual_risks: Sampling is uniform on labeled words, not on necklaces. The asymptotic is not uniform in growing g or near endpoint densities.

evidence: Whiteland's searchable chapter description indicates an auxiliary-word conjugacy equation in §4; the full text was not retrieved and is not used to clear this source. Independently, existential auxiliary-word conjugacy is not pairwise signature equality on actual rotations: x=01,y=10 have distinct signatures, but xz=zy for z=0.
The target expectation adds uniform fixed-content arc counts, inclusion–exclusion of r-way equalities for arbitrary r through g, and uniform Stirling summed over cyclic pair distances.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The verified class formulas and g=2 mean do not imply those joint probabilities for all g. A result about existence of a word z would not alone give fixed-length rotational class diversity; explicit overlap with uninspected details of the chapter remains a residual risk.

Binary linear-word equivalence, the deterministic lower-bound characterization, and the g=2 moment and asymptotic are not counted as distinct from their inspected matches. value.rationale: The observable measures how many distinct observations remain when the start of a fixed-composition circular word is unknown. Neither deterministic bounds nor the g=2 exact result quantifies the typical loss at general gcd. The gap-product expression supplies such a mean for all fixed compositions, and its explicit square-root correction distinguishes pair collisions from higher-order coincidences; both are useful beyond the matching deterministic criterion.
residual_risks: The exact formula can grow exponentially in g; the result does not give the full distribution at general gcd or a reconstruction method.
